items.headline: Sensex jumps 905 points to 74,151.04 and Nifty 1.05% to 22,936.75 after the Fed holds
items.summary: Midcaps rose 0.99% and smallcaps 0.95%. Drivers: the Fed pause, a firmer rupee and talk of a capital gains tax review, though nothing is announced. Reverses Wednesday's fall.
items.rationale: Relief on global rates and hopes for lower investor taxes lift sentiment, but analysts flag crude, rupee weakness and high bond yields as headwinds that could cap the rebound.

items.headline: Foreign investors sell a net ₹944 crore; domestic funds buy ₹1,924 crore (provisional)
items.summary: Foreign selling returns after two days of buying, even as the market rallied. Domestic buying again carried the day. Reversing back to outflows.
items.rationale: Foreign selling on an up day shows overseas appetite remains fragile while oil is high; steady domestic inflows cushion stocks.

items.headline: 10-year G-Sec yield falls about 5 basis points to 7.39–7.40%, its sharpest drop since July
items.summary: Down from 7.44% as US Treasuries rallied after the Fed and crude eased slightly. Eases pressure after yields hit their highest since 2023 this week. Easing.
items.rationale: Lower yields cut borrowing costs and lift banks' bond portfolios; the relief may not last if oil climbs again.

items.headline: Rupee edges up 2 paise to 95.26 per dollar after touching 95.38
items.summary: A slightly hawkish Fed and strong dollar weighed, but the stock rally and softer crude limited losses. Steadies after Wednesday's 21-paise fall. Ongoing pressure.
items.rationale: A stable but weak rupee keeps imported oil and inputs costly while supporting exporters' earnings.

items.headline: Iran declares Hormuz closed after a tanker fire; Guard says three tankers hit mines on a southern route
items.summary: Iran disputes US claims that lanes were swept. Transits were 2 a day on 25 October against 85 before the war. Brent heads for an 11% monthly gain. Escalating.
items.rationale: A renewed closure keeps oil and LNG supply risk high for India, lifting import costs, freight and insurance, and pressuring the rupee and inflation.

items.headline: US vice president writes to Iran proposing an early meeting; Tehran insists on its seven conditions
items.summary: Iranian media say the letter was received but not answered. Comes days after reports the US told Gulf states to prepare for post-election strikes. Mixed signals; diplomacy ongoing.
items.rationale: Direct talks would be the clearest path to lower oil for India, but conditions and strike planning keep the outcome uncertain.

items.headline: Commerce minister says the US trade deal protects sensitive interests and gives India a strong advantage
items.summary: He said details are not yet public and people will celebrate the terms. Follows weeks of talks reported as close but stuck. Progressing.
items.rationale: A deal with lower US tariffs would help exporters of textiles, engineering goods and farm products and improve the trade outlook.

items.headline: India's LNG imports from Qatar surge nearly 370% in October as supplies recover
items.summary: Adds to expected record October LNG imports of 2.8 million tonnes. Recovery from earlier disruption, though at high prices and now threatened by Iran's renewed closure.
items.rationale: More gas supports power, fertiliser and city gas, but high prices raise the import bill and any new Hormuz closure risks the flow.
